title: WHO: 4.9 million children under 5 died in 2024
summary: WHO's child-mortality sheet says that was 37.4 deaths per 1,000 live births, and that 2.3 million of the deaths were in the first 28 days.
body: WHO's under-five mortality fact sheet, dated 1 May 2026, says that in 2024 an estimated 4.9 million children under 5 died, equivalent to one death every 6 seconds. It says neonatal deaths, the first 28 days, accounted for 2.3 million, 47 percent of under-five deaths. It says the global under-five mortality rate declined to 37.4 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2024, less than half its level in 2000. It says children born in sub-Saharan Africa had a rate of 71.6 per 1,000, nearly 14 times the rate in Europe and Northern America, and that sub-Saharan Africa and Southern Asia together accounted for more than 80 percent of under-five deaths in 2024. It names the leading causes as preterm birth complications, intrapartum-related events such as birth asphyxia or trauma, pneumonia, diarrhoea, and malaria, and it says these are largely preventable or treatable. The figures are the sheet's 2024 estimates.
